title: Staged signoff ladder and dependency triage for PRD clarity
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: This ticket formalizes a staged signoff ladder for the new PRD (Staged Responses & Fallthroughs) to reduce back-and-forth during final acceptance. Multiple recent PRDs have stalled because signoffs were requested as a single monolithic gate; this ticket pilots a phased approach where design, engineering, and legal sign off incrementally against a shared checklist.

Scope:
- Create a single canonical acceptance checklist with discrete items that each team can approve independently.
- Define who signs which checklist rows, what artifacts are required for each signoff (mockups, API contract, dataflow diagram, legal playbook), and expected SLA for review (3 business days for design, 5 business days for engineering, 7 business days for legal).
- Add a lightweight rollout gating matrix that maps checklist rows to rollout controls (feature flag, canary %, telemetry dashboards).

Out of scope: full process automation (we will start with a Google Sheet + templates), changes to broader company signoff policy.

Decisions & trade-offs so far:
- Trade-off chosen: keep signoff artifacts human-readable (Confluence + shared drive) rather than building a heavy workflow in the Console right away to iterate quickly.
- Agreement with Legal: redline-style contract review is required only for features that touch customer data or contractual obligations; otherwise a scoped legal checklist is sufficient.
- Engineering asked to provide an API compatibility statement (backwards-compatible? migration steps?) before final engineering signoff.

Artifacts (links):
- PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PM/Staged+Responses+PRD+Draft
- Acceptance checklist template: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1staged-acceptance-template
- Design mocks (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/abc-staged-responses
- Initial engineering contract (proto): https://github.com/redwood-inference/staged-responses/pull/92

Why this matters: A discrete signoff ladder reduces blocking and makes responsibilities explicit. For Dedicated and Private customers the legal/ops items are the most common blockers; surfacing them earlier avoids late surprises in release planning.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical acceptance checklist created and published in Confluence and linked in the PRD
Each checklist row has: owning team, required artifact link, expected review SLA, and gating action (none/flag/canary/hold)
Design signoff path: Design approves mocks + accessibility checks; approval captured in checklist with timestamp
Engineering signoff path: API contract sketch, expected throughput/latency implications, migration plan for existing customers; captured in checklist
Legal signoff path: data processing assessment done for PII-sensitive flows; either legal approves or opens a redline task with next steps
At least one internal pilot PRD (this one) completes the ladder with all three teams' approvals and is allowed to proceed to a canary rollout
Rollout gating matrix is added to the PRD and maps to an observability dashboard with at least 3 KPIs (errors, p50 latency, token cost delta)
A retrospective note is created after pilot signoff describing friction points and proposed process updates
